In the devdesk Go repo, I need a precise inventory of every GitLab and GitHub API operation the app actually performs, so I can verify whether the token scopes documented in internal/forge/vocabulary.go (GitLab: "api, write_repository, read_repository"; GitHub: "repo, read:org") are correct — neither too narrow (missing an operation) nor unnecessarily broad.

Please investigate (read-only, report back, do not write code):

1. Read `internal/forge/forge.go` (the `Forge` interface) fully — every method it declares.
2. Read every file in `internal/forge/gitlab/` fully. For each method, note exactly which `gitlab.com/gitlab-org/api/client-go` client service and method it calls (e.g. `client.Projects.ListProjects`, `client.Groups.CreateGroup`, `client.Users.CurrentUser`, `client.MergeRequests.CreateMergeRequest`, etc.) — list every distinct API call made, including anything used only for cloning (does it use the API to get a clone URL, or does clone go straight through git over HTTPS/SSH without an API call?).
3. Read every file in `internal/forge/github/` fully, same treatment for `github.com/google/go-github/v68` calls.
4. Check `internal/forge/session/session.go` for what `CurrentUser` calls each backend makes as the "connection test".
5. Report a plain list per backend: every distinct operation (read project/repo list, read group/org list, create project/repo, create group/org — does this exist?, create merge request/pull request, read merge request/pull request status or list, clone, current user, anything else) with the exact client-go/go-github method name used for each.

Do not look up or state scope requirements yourself — just give me the exhaustive list of operations performed, with method names, so I can reason about the scopes separately. Keep the report factual and concise, organized as two lists (GitLab operations, GitHub operations) with file:line references.

1	// Package forge is what DevDesk asks of a code-hosting platform.
2	//
3	// It exists so a configuration context can target GitLab or GitHub — exactly
4	// one of the two, never both (§3.6). Everything above it speaks this
5	// vocabulary; only the backends know which SDK is underneath.
6	//
7	// # It is derived from what the code consumes, not from what an API offers
8	//
9	// Every method here answers a call site that exists today: the auth view wants
10	// the current user, the explorer browses and creates and deletes, the clone
11	// pipeline walks and builds URLs, the dashboard counts. Nothing was added
12	// because a forge happens to expose it. A method with no caller is a promise
13	// nobody checks, and two backends would honour it two different ways before
14	// anyone noticed.
15	//
16	// # A backend declares its shape
17	//
18	// The two forges differ in *words* and in *shapes*, and only the first is a
19	// presentation problem — Vocabulary handles those, and it is not in this
20	// package. A shape is what the abstraction can promise at all: how deep
21	// namespaces nest, which visibilities exist, whether a delete can be made
22	// permanent. Those are Shape, returned by the backend and never guessed from a
23	// URL — the registry `provider` field is the precedent (§3.8).
24	//
25	// # Identity is opaque; the path is not
26	//
27	// A namespace or a repository carries two strings. ID addresses it with the
28	// backend and means nothing outside: GitLab needs a number to create under a
29	// parent (CreateGroupOptions.ParentID is an *int64), GitHub addresses by owner.
30	// Path is the human one — `group/subgroup`, `owner/repo` — and it is what the
31	// clone URL, the display and GitLab's renamed-path deletion are built from.
32	//
33	// A caller that parses an ID is a caller bound to one forge. The type is a
34	// string so that arithmetic on it cannot be written.
35	//
36	// # A namespace and a repository are different types
37	//
38	// Not one node with a kind field. Only a namespace has children; only a
39	// repository has a pipeline status and a deletion schedule. Distinct types make
40	// "drill into a repository" unexpressible rather than forbidden by review —
41	// the same trade datatable's `Cell func(T) string` makes for Rule 122.
42	//
43	// The explorer still renders them in one table, and still holds its own
44	// TreeNode for what a *tree* needs — expanded, loading, parent, depth. Those
45	// are view state, and a forge has no opinion on them.
46	//
47	// # The backend paginates, and the caller never sees a page
48	//
49	// D34 was four copies of `PerPage: 100, Page: 1`, so a group with more than a
50	// hundred children was silently cut. A list returned here is complete or it is
51	// an error; there is no page to forget.
52	//
53	// # Every call takes a context
54	//
55	// The clone's discovery is cancellable and its clones are not (§3.16), which is
56	// a distinction the caller can only make if the reads take a context. Today
57	// every call passes context.Background(); that is what this fixes.
58	package forge
59	
60	import "context"
61	
62	// Forge is one code-hosting backend, bound to one host and one token.
63	//
64	// A consumer should declare the subset it needs rather than depend on this
65	// whole interface — Go resolves that at the consumer, so the backend does not
66	// have to be split. The dashboard wants DashboardStats and nothing else.
67	type Forge interface {
68		// Shape reports what this backend can express. It is a value, not a
69		// request: nothing about it depends on the network or on the token.
70		Shape() Shape
71	
72		// CurrentUser is who the token belongs to. It is also the connection test:
73		// authentication succeeded exactly when this returns.
74		CurrentUser(ctx context.Context) (User, error)
75	
76		// RootNamespaces lists the top-level namespaces the user can see — GitLab's
77		// top-level groups, GitHub's organisations. Complete, every page.
78		RootNamespaces(ctx context.Context, opts BrowseOptions) ([]Namespace, error)
79	
80		// Children lists one namespace's direct children, complete.
81		//
82		// Direct, not recursive: the explorer drills one level at a time and the
83		// clone walks levels itself, so a recursive listing would fetch what
84		// neither asked for.
85		Children(ctx context.Context, namespaceID string, opts BrowseOptions) (Children, error)
86	
87		// CreateNamespace creates a namespace, optionally under a parent. A backend
88		// whose Shape refuses the requested depth returns an error rather than
89		// creating it at the root.
90		CreateNamespace(ctx context.Context, spec NewNamespace) (Namespace, error)
91	
92		// CreateRepository creates a repository inside a namespace.
93		CreateRepository(ctx context.Context, spec NewRepository) (Repository, error)
94	
95		// InitialCommit writes the first commit of a repository — what a template
96		// is applied by. It is separate from CreateRepository because a repository
97		// is created whether or not a template was chosen.
98		InitialCommit(ctx context.Context, repositoryID string, files []FileChange) error
99	
100		// DeleteNamespace deletes a namespace and everything under it.
101		//
102		// It takes the whole value rather than an ID because permanent deletion
103		// needs both: GitLab schedules the deletion, which *renames* the namespace
104		// to `<path>-deletion_scheduled-<id>`, and the second call addresses that
105		// new path. A backend whose Shape says PermanentDelete is false returns an
106		// error when asked for one, rather than deleting normally and reporting
107		// success for something else.
108		DeleteNamespace(ctx context.Context, ns Namespace, permanently bool) error
109	
110		// DeleteRepository deletes a repository. Same two-argument reasoning as
111		// DeleteNamespace.
112		DeleteRepository(ctx context.Context, repo Repository, permanently bool) error
113	
114		// DashboardStats fetches the dashboard's counters for one user.
115		DashboardStats(ctx context.Context, user User) (DashboardStats, error)
116	
117		// CloneURL is the git URL for a repository. No network, no token: it is
118		// built from the host, the path and the method, and the token travels
119		// through git's environment rather than through the URL (§3.16).
120		CloneURL(repo Repository, method CloneMethod) string
121	
122		// ChangeRequestsURL is the web page listing the user's merge or pull
123		// requests, and AssignedIssuesURL the one listing their open issues.
124		//
125		// They are on the backend because the paths differ per forge and the views
126		// used to build them with fmt.Sprintf against the configured URL — which is
127		// a forge shape written in a view.
128		// MergedCIConfig is the CI configuration the forge derives from the
129		// repository: every include and component resolved, as the pipeline would
130		// run. repoID addresses the repository the way the backend does, ref names
131		// the branch — empty means the default one.
132		//
133		// It is the server's answer and not a local expansion, deliberately:
134		// resolving includes here would mean re-implementing the forge's own CI
135		// engine, and being wrong somewhere without knowing where.
136		//
137		// A backend whose Shape says MergedCIConfig is false returns an error
138		// naming the reason. Callers gate on the shape rather than on the error —
139		// the error is what a caller that forgot gets, not the way to ask.
140		MergedCIConfig(ctx context.Context, repoID, ref string) (string, error)
141	
142		ChangeRequestsURL() string
143		AssignedIssuesURL(user User) string
144	}

1	// Package gitlab is the GitLab backend of internal/forge.
2	//
3	// It is the only place in DevDesk that knows go-gitlab exists. Everything it
4	// exports is either forge's vocabulary or the constructor that binds a host and
5	// a token to it.
6	//
7	// # What it hides
8	//
9	// Pagination (D34), the numeric identifiers GitLab wants where a path will not
10	// do, the two-step permanent delete and its renamed path, and the mapping from
11	// GitLab's numeric access levels to a word. Each of those leaked into a view
12	// before this package existed, and each is the kind of thing a second forge
13	// would have contradicted quietly.
14	package gitlab
15	
16	import (
17		"context"
18		"fmt"
19		"log"
20		"net/url"
21		"strings"
22		"sync"
23		"time"
24	
25		gitlabclient "gitlab.com/gitlab-org/api/client-go"
26	
27		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/config"
28		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/forge"
29	)
30	
31	// Forge is a GitLab instance, bound to one host and one token.
32	type Forge struct {
33		client *gitlabclient.Client
34		// mu guards user, the memoised answer to CurrentUser. The clone pipeline
35		// calls into the backend from several goroutines, so this is a real race
36		// rather than a theoretical one.
37		mu   sync.Mutex
38		user *forge.User
39		// baseURL is the host as the user configured it, trailing slash removed.
40		// The SDK holds its own API base; this one builds clone URLs and web links,
41		// which are not API paths.
42		baseURL string
43	}
44	
45	var _ forge.Forge = (*Forge)(nil)
46	
47	// New binds a GitLab instance to a token.
48	func New(baseURL, token string) (*Forge, error) {
49		client, err := gitlabclient.NewClient(token, gitlabclient.WithBaseURL(baseURL))
50		if err != nil {
51			return nil, err
52		}
53		return NewWithClient(client, baseURL), nil
54	}
55	
56	// NewWithClient wraps a client that already exists, or none at all.
57	//
58	// A nil client is legitimate: CloneURL, ChangeRequestsURL and AssignedIssuesURL
59	// are built from the host and touch nothing, so they answer without a session.
60	func NewWithClient(client *gitlabclient.Client, baseURL string) *Forge {
61		return &Forge{client: client, baseURL: strings.TrimSuffix(baseURL, "/")}
62	}
63	
64	// Shape is GitLab's, and it is a constant: nothing about it depends on the
65	// instance or on the token.
66	//
67	// It delegates to forge.ShapeFor so there is one table rather than two. A shape
68	// is a property of the platform, and the configuration view needs it before any
69	// session exists — this method is for a consumer that holds a session and does
70	// not know the type.
71	func (f *Forge) Shape() forge.Shape {
72		return forge.ShapeFor(config.ForgeGitLab)
73	}
74	
75	// CurrentUser is who the token belongs to, and the connection test with it.
76	// It is memoised, and that is not an optimisation. Every decorated listing
77	// needs the caller's id for its role lookups; asking the host each time would
78	// add one request per listing that the pre-abstraction code did not make,
79	// because it took the id from a session the view was already holding. Who a
80	// token belongs to does not change for the life of a session.
81	func (f *Forge) CurrentUser(ctx context.Context) (forge.User, error) {
82		f.mu.Lock()
83		if f.user != nil {
84			defer f.mu.Unlock()
85			return *f.user, nil
86		}
87		f.mu.Unlock()
88	
89		user, _, err := f.client.Users.CurrentUser(gitlabclient.WithContext(ctx))
90		if err != nil {
91			return forge.User{}, err
92		}
93		resolved := forge.User{
94			ID:       fmt.Sprint(user.ID),
95			Username: user.Username,
96			Name:     user.Name,
97		}
98	
99		f.mu.Lock()
100		f.user = &resolved
101		f.mu.Unlock()
102		return resolved, nil
103	}
104	
105	// CloneURL builds the git URL. No network and no token: the token travels
106	// through git's environment, never in the URL (§3.16).
107	func (f *Forge) CloneURL(repo forge.Repository, method forge.CloneMethod) string {
108		if method == forge.CloneSSH {
109			host := strings.TrimPrefix(strings.TrimPrefix(f.baseURL, "https://"), "http://")
110			return fmt.Sprintf("git@%s:%s.git", host, repo.Path)
111		}
112		return fmt.Sprintf("%s/%s.git", f.baseURL, repo.Path)
113	}
114	
115	// ChangeRequestsURL is GitLab's merge request dashboard.
116	func (f *Forge) ChangeRequestsURL() string {
117		return f.baseURL + "/dashboard/merge_requests"
118	}
119	
120	// AssignedIssuesURL is the issue dashboard filtered to one assignee.
121	//
122	// The username is escaped rather than interpolated raw: it reaches this from
123	// the API, but a URL built by concatenation is how a query parameter ends up
124	// meaning something else, and nothing about the call site says the value is
125	// safe.
126	func (f *Forge) AssignedIssuesURL(user forge.User) string {
127		q := url.Values{
128			"sort":                {"created_date"},
129			"state":               {"opened"},
130			"assignee_username[]": {user.Username},
131		}
132		return f.baseURL + "/dashboard/issues?" + q.Encode()
133	}
134	
135	// roleName turns a GitLab access level into the word forge.Namespace.Role
136	// promises. It is the mapping TreeNode.AccessLevelName held, moved to the only
137	// place that knows what a 40 means.
138	//
139	// Zero is "not known" and returns the empty string — not "Guest". A role the
140	// backend could not read is not the lowest role there is.
141	func roleName(level int) string {
142		switch {
143		case level >= 50:
144			return "Owner"
145		case level >= 40:
146			return "Maintainer"
147		case level >= 30:
148			return "Developer"
149		case level >= 20:
150			return "Reporter"
151		case level >= 10:
152			return "Guest"
153		default:
154			return ""
155		}
156	}
157	
158	// namespaceID renders a GitLab numeric ID as the opaque string forge uses.
159	func namespaceID(id int64) string { return fmt.Sprint(id) }
160	
161	// numericID reads back what namespaceID wrote.
162	//
163	// Only this package may do it — that is the package doc's rule, and the reason
164	// forge.Namespace.ID is a string is so that no caller outside can. GitLab needs
165	// the number in two places where a path is not accepted: CreateGroupOptions
166	// .ParentID and CreateProjectOptions.NamespaceID are both *int64.
167	func numericID(id string) (int64, error) {
168		var n int64
169		if _, err := fmt.Sscanf(id, "%d", &n); err != nil {
170			return 0, fmt.Errorf("not a GitLab id: %q", id)
171		}
172		return n, nil
173	}
174	
175	// deletionPath is what GitLab renames a group or project to when a deletion is
176	// scheduled. The permanent removal addresses that name, not the original.
177	func deletionPath(path string, id int64) string {
178		return fmt.Sprintf("%s-deletion_scheduled-%d", path, id)
179	}
180	
181	// propagationDelay is the pause between scheduling a deletion and asking for
182	// the permanent removal.
183	//
184	// It was in the code being moved, undocumented. It is kept because removing it
185	// would be an unrelated behaviour change inside a refactor that promises none —
186	// not because 500 ms is known to be the right number.
187	const propagationDelay = 500 * time.Millisecond
188	
189	// MergedCIConfig is the pipeline as GitLab resolves it: every `include` and
190	// every component expanded server-side, which is what a plumber finding is

194	// resolved document and the transitive include graph, and neither is derivable
195	// from the repository alone — a single `include:` in a fifteen-line file
196	// resolves to fifteen includes and twenty-one jobs on a measured example.

199	// what the user came to read, and a lint failure is often precisely why. The
200	// errors go to the log, the YAML comes back if there is one, and an empty
201	// document is the one case that fails — there is nothing to show.
202	func (f *Forge) MergedCIConfig(ctx context.Context, repoID, ref string) (string, error) {

204		if ref != "" {
205			opts.Ref = gitlabclient.Ptr(ref)
206		}
207		result, _, err := f.client.Validate.ProjectLint(repoID, opts, gitlabclient.WithContext(ctx))
208		if err != nil {
209			return "", fmt.Errorf("resolve CI configuration for %s: %w", repoID, err)

211		if !result.Valid {
212			log.Printf("WARN [forge/gitlab] %s: the resolved CI configuration is invalid: %s",

216			return "", fmt.Errorf("resolve CI configuration for %s: the server returned no document", repoID)

4	// sibling is the only place that knows go-gitlab.

6	// # What it does not do, and says so
7	//
8	// GitHub has no API for creating or deleting an **organisation**, and no grace
9	// period a delete could bypass. The interface expects a backend to refuse what
10	// its Shape says it cannot express rather than to do something adjacent and
11	// report success — so both come back as errors naming the reason, and the
12	// permanent-delete checkbox is out of reach because `Shape.PermanentDelete` is
13	// false.
14	//
15	// # Identity is the path
16	//
17	// forge.Namespace.ID is opaque, which lets each backend pick what addresses an
18	// object. GitLab needs a number in two places; GitHub needs `owner` and
19	// `owner/repo` everywhere, so here ID and Path are the same string. Nothing
20	// outside this package may notice.
21	package github

23	import (
24		"context"
25		"errors"
26		"fmt"

37	// Forge is a GitHub instance — github.com or an Enterprise Server — bound to
38	// one token.
39	type Forge struct {
40		client *gh.Client
41		// baseURL is the *web* host as the user configured it. The SDK holds its
42		// own API base, which on Enterprise is a different path; this one builds
43		// clone URLs and browser links.
44		baseURL string
45	
46		mu   sync.Mutex
47		user *forge.User
48	}

50	var _ forge.Forge = (*Forge)(nil)

52	// New binds a GitHub instance to a token.
53	//
54	// A host other than github.com is taken as GitHub Enterprise Server, whose API
55	// lives under /api/v3/ — WithEnterpriseURLs appends that, so the configured URL
56	// stays the web host the user typed and the one clone URLs are built from.
57	func New(baseURL, token string) (*Forge, error) {
58		client := gh.NewClient(nil).WithAuthToken(token)
59	
60		trimmed := strings.TrimSuffix(baseURL, "/")
61		if !isDotCom(trimmed) && trimmed != "" {
62			enterprise, err := client.WithEnterpriseURLs(trimmed, trimmed)
63			if err != nil {
64				return nil, fmt.Errorf("github enterprise URL: %w", err)
65			}
66			client = enterprise
67		}
68	
69		return &Forge{client: client, baseURL: trimmed}, nil
70	}

72	// NewWithClient wraps a client that already exists, or none at all. A nil
73	// client is legitimate: the URL helpers touch nothing.
74	func NewWithClient(client *gh.Client, baseURL string) *Forge {
75		return &Forge{client: client, baseURL: strings.TrimSuffix(baseURL, "/")}
76	}

78	// isDotCom reports whether a URL names the public instance.
79	func isDotCom(rawURL string) bool {
80		host := strings.TrimPrefix(strings.TrimPrefix(rawURL, "https://"), "http://")
81		host, _, _ = strings.Cut(host, "/")
82		return host == "" || host == "github.com" || host == "www.github.com"
83	}

85	// Shape delegates, so the platform's capabilities are declared once (§3.6
86	// step 6). GitHub's are the interesting half of the abstraction: no nesting, no
87	// `internal`, no permanent delete.
88	func (f *Forge) Shape() forge.Shape {
89		return forge.ShapeFor(config.ForgeGitHub)

92	// CurrentUser is who the token belongs to, and the connection test with it.
93	//
94	// Memoised for its GitLab sibling's reason: every decorated listing needs the
95	// caller's login for its role lookups, and asking the host each time would add
96	// a request per listing.
97	func (f *Forge) CurrentUser(ctx context.Context) (forge.User, error) {
98		f.mu.Lock()
99		if f.user != nil {
100			defer f.mu.Unlock()
101			return *f.user, nil
102		}
103		f.mu.Unlock()
104	
105		user, _, err := f.client.Users.Get(ctx, "")
106		if err != nil {
107			return forge.User{}, err
108		}
109	
110		// The login, not the numeric id: it is what every other call addresses a
111		// user by, and forge.User.ID is opaque precisely so a backend can choose.
112		resolved := forge.User{
113			ID:       user.GetLogin(),
114			Username: user.GetLogin(),
115			Name:     user.GetName(),
116		}
117	
118		f.mu.Lock()
119		f.user = &resolved
120		f.mu.Unlock()

124	// CloneURL builds the git URL from the web host, the path and the method.
125	func (f *Forge) CloneURL(repo forge.Repository, method forge.CloneMethod) string {
126		base := f.webBase()
127		if method == forge.CloneSSH {
128			host := strings.TrimPrefix(strings.TrimPrefix(base, "https://"), "http://")
129			return fmt.Sprintf("git@%s:%s.git", host, repo.Path)
130		}
131		return fmt.Sprintf("%s/%s.git", base, repo.Path)
132	}

134	// ChangeRequestsURL is GitHub's pull request dashboard.

140	// parameter — which is exactly why it is escaped rather than concatenated.
141	func (f *Forge) AssignedIssuesURL(user forge.User) string {
142		q := url.Values{"q": {"is:open is:issue assignee:" + user.Username}}
143		return f.webBase() + "/issues?" + q.Encode()

146	// webBase is the host browser links and clone URLs are built from. An empty
147	// configured URL means github.com, which is the only host that has a default.
148	func (f *Forge) webBase() string {
149		if f.baseURL == "" {
150			return "https://github.com"
151		}
152		return f.baseURL
153	}

155	// MergedCIConfig is refused: GitHub has no equivalent.
156	//
157	// A workflow's `uses:` is resolved by the runner when the job starts, so there
158	// is no endpoint that hands back an expanded workflow — and answering with the
159	// raw `.github/workflows/*.yml` would report a distinction the platform does

161	// permanent delete here.

164	// reaches this. It exists for the one that forgot.
165	func (f *Forge) MergedCIConfig(_ context.Context, _, _ string) (string, error) {
166		return "", errors.New("GitHub resolves a workflow's `uses:` when the runner starts it, so there is no resolved configuration to fetch")
167	}

15	// listAll walks every page and returns the lot — D34's rule, applied to the
16	// second backend before it can go wrong here too.
17	//
18	// GitHub paginates by Link header, which go-github surfaces as
19	// Response.NextPage, 0 on the last page. The guard against a server that keeps
20	// pointing at the page just served is the GitLab backend's, for the same
21	// reason: it cannot cut a legitimate response short, which a page cap would.
22	func listAll[T any](fetch func(opts *gh.ListOptions) ([]T, *gh.Response, error)) ([]T, error) {
23		opts := &gh.ListOptions{PerPage: perPage, Page: 1}
24	
25		var all []T
26		for {
27			page, resp, err := fetch(opts)
28			if err != nil {
29				return nil, err
30			}
31			all = append(all, page...)
32	
33			if resp == nil || resp.NextPage <= opts.Page {
34				return all, nil
35			}
36			opts.Page = resp.NextPage
37		}
38	}

40	// RootNamespaces lists the user's own account, then the organisations the token
41	// can see.
42	//
43	// **The personal account comes first, and leaving it out was a bug.** The first
44	// version of this excluded it, reasoning that "a personal namespace is not an
45	// organisation: it cannot be created or deleted, so listing it would put a row
46	// in the tree that half the actions refuse". That is wrong on its own terms —
47	// *no* GitHub organisation can be created or deleted through the API, so the
48	// personal account is not less capable than an organisation but **more**: it is
49	// the one namespace where a repository can be created and deleted.
50	//
51	// The cost of the mistake was the common case. A personal GitHub account
52	// belongs to no organisation, so the explorer opened empty and said so, on the
53	// account shape most people have.
54	func (f *Forge) RootNamespaces(ctx context.Context, opts forge.BrowseOptions) ([]forge.Namespace, error) {
55		orgs, err := listAll(func(page *gh.ListOptions) ([]*gh.Organization, *gh.Response, error) {
56			return f.client.Organizations.List(ctx, "", page)

65		// solo account's repositories are, and burying it under a list of
66		// organisations would hide the only row half of them have.

68			return append([]forge.Namespace{personal}, namespaces...), nil

163	// namespaces converts organisations.
164	func (f *Forge) namespaces(ctx context.Context, orgs []*gh.Organization, login string) []forge.Namespace {
165		out := make([]forge.Namespace, 0, len(orgs))
166		for _, org := range orgs {
167			created := org.GetCreatedAt().Time
168			ns := forge.Namespace{
169				ID:     org.GetLogin(),
170				Path:   org.GetLogin(),
171				Name:   firstNonEmpty(org.GetName(), org.GetLogin()),
172				WebURL: f.webBase() + "/" + org.GetLogin(),
173				// An organisation has no visibility of its own on GitHub — its
174				// repositories do. Left empty rather than invented.
175				CreatedAt: &created,
176			}
177			if login != "" {
178				ns.Role = f.orgRole(ctx, org.GetLogin(), login)

185	// repositories converts repositories, decorating each with the caller's role

189	// walk asks for none of it.
190	func (f *Forge) repositories(ctx context.Context, repos []*gh.Repository, login string) []forge.Repository {
191		out := make([]forge.Repository, 0, len(repos))
192		for _, repo := range repos {
193			created, pushed := repo.GetCreatedAt().Time, repo.GetPushedAt().Time
194			full := repo.GetFullName()

196			converted := forge.Repository{
197				ID:             full,
198				Path:           full,
199				Name:           repo.GetName(),
200				Visibility:     visibilityOf(repo),
201				CreatedAt:      &created,
202				LastActivityAt: &pushed,
203				WebURL:         repo.GetHTMLURL(),
204				// GitHub deletes at once, so a repository is never *scheduled* for
205				// deletion. Always false, and Shape.PermanentDelete says why.
206				DeletionScheduled: false,

208			if login != "" {

210				converted.CIStatus = f.lastWorkflowStatus(ctx, repo.GetOwner().GetLogin(), repo.GetName())

220	// older boolean github.com always sets. Reading the first and falling back to
221	// the second is what keeps an Enterprise `internal` from being reported as
222	// `private` — a visibility this platform's Shape does not offer for creation,
223	// but which an Enterprise instance really has.
224	func visibilityOf(repo *gh.Repository) string {
225		if v := repo.GetVisibility(); v != "" {
226			return v
227		}

235	// forge.Repository.Role promises.

238	// most-privileged first. Nothing means the permissions were not returned, which

240	func roleName(perms map[string]bool) string {
241		switch {
242		case perms["admin"]:
243			return "Owner"
244		case perms["maintain"]:
245			return "Maintainer"
246		case perms["push"]:
247			return "Developer"
248		case perms["triage"]:
249			return "Reporter"
250		case perms["pull"]:
251			return "Guest"

270		if membership.GetRole() == "admin" {

276	// lastWorkflowStatus is the most recent Actions run, translated into the
277	// vocabulary forge.CIStatus* declares.
278	//
279	// A run still in flight has no conclusion, so its *status* is used instead —
280	// otherwise a repository whose build is running would read as having no CI at
281	// all. The two are different alphabets, which is why ciStatusOf takes both and
282	// not one string.
283	//
284	// It was called lastWorkflowConclusion and claimed to return "the same words
285	// the GitLab backend reports". It never did (D66): only `success` and `skipped`
286	// happen to be spelled the same, so `failure` reached the CI column as raw text
287	// truncated to `failu…` and coloured orange by the view's default branch — a
288	// broken build rendered as a warning, which is the one thing that column exists
289	// to prevent.
290	func (f *Forge) lastWorkflowStatus(ctx context.Context, owner, repo string) string {
291		runs, _, err := f.client.Actions.ListRepositoryWorkflowRuns(ctx, owner, repo,
292			&gh.ListWorkflowRunsOptions{ListOptions: gh.ListOptions{PerPage: 1, Page: 1}})
293		if err != nil || runs == nil || len(runs.WorkflowRuns) == 0 {
294			return ""
295		}
296	
297		run := runs.WorkflowRuns[0]
298		return ciStatusOf(run.GetConclusion(), run.GetStatus())
299	}

301	// ciStatusOf translates one Actions run onto forge's vocabulary.
302	//
303	// The conclusion is read first and the status only when there is none: a
304	// completed run carries both, and its `completed` status says nothing a reader
305	// wants — which is precisely why `completed` appears in neither table below.
306	//
307	// **An unrecognised value returns the empty string**, not itself. That is what
308	// forge.Repository.CIStatus documents for a value the backend has no equivalent
309	// for, and it is the difference between an empty cell and six characters of
310	// GitHub's internal spelling. Returning the raw word was the defect.
311	func ciStatusOf(conclusion, status string) string {
312		if conclusion != "" {
313			return ciConclusions[conclusion]
314		}
315		return ciRunStates[status]
316	}

318	// ciConclusions maps a finished run. Four of GitHub's nine outcomes have no
319	// counterpart and are folded rather than dropped, each on its own argument:
320	//
321	//   - `timed_out` and `startup_failure` are **failures**. GitLab has no separate
322	//     status for either — a job it kills on timeout ends `failed` — so folding
323	//     them is reporting what GitLab would have reported, not losing detail.
324	//   - `action_required` is a run waiting for someone to approve it, which is
325	//     exactly what GitLab calls `manual`.
326	//   - `neutral` and `stale` are the grey outcomes: ran without a verdict, and
327	//     superseded before finishing. GitHub renders both the way it renders
328	//     `skipped`, and `skipped` is the only grey this vocabulary has.
329	var ciConclusions = map[string]string{
330		"success":         forge.CIStatusSuccess,
331		"failure":         forge.CIStatusFailed,
332		"timed_out":       forge.CIStatusFailed,
333		"startup_failure": forge.CIStatusFailed,
334		"cancelled":       forge.CIStatusCanceled, // GitHub spells it with two l's
335		"action_required": forge.CIStatusManual,
336		"skipped":         forge.CIStatusSkipped,
337		"neutral":         forge.CIStatusSkipped,
338		"stale":           forge.CIStatusSkipped,
339	}
340	
341	// ciRunStates maps a run that has not finished. GitLab separates `pending` from
342	// `created`, `preparing` and `waiting_for_resource`; GitHub's four pre-run
343	// states all mean the same thing to a reader — it has not started — so they
344	// collapse onto the one word the CI column already draws a clock for.
345	var ciRunStates = map[string]string{
346		"in_progress": forge.CIStatusRunning,
347		"queued":      forge.CIStatusPending,
348		"requested":   forge.CIStatusPending,
349		"waiting":     forge.CIStatusPending,
350		"pending":     forge.CIStatusPending,
351	}
352	
353	// splitPath cuts an owner/repo identifier.
354	//
355	// GitHub addresses a repository by its two halves in every write call, and this
356	// is the one place that knows the identifier has halves at all — outside this
357	// package it is opaque.
358	func splitPath(id string) (owner, repo string, ok bool) {
359		owner, repo, ok = strings.Cut(id, "/")
360		return owner, repo, ok && owner != "" && repo != ""
361	}
362	
363	func firstNonEmpty(values ...string) string {
364		for _, v := range values {
365			if v != "" {
366				return v
367			}
368		}
369		return ""
370	}

45	func (f *Forge) CreateRepository(ctx context.Context, spec forge.NewRepository) (forge.Repository, error) {
46		shape := f.Shape()
47		if spec.Visibility != "" && !shape.AllowsVisibility(spec.Visibility) {
48			return forge.Repository{}, fmt.Errorf("GitHub does not offer %q visibility", spec.Visibility)
49		}

51		created, _, err := f.client.Repositories.Create(ctx, spec.NamespaceID, &gh.Repository{
52			Name:        gh.Ptr(spec.Slug),
53			Description: gh.Ptr(spec.Description),
54			Private:     gh.Ptr(spec.Visibility != "public"),

56			// commit, and an auto-generated README would give it a parent it does
57			// not expect — the two would race to own the initial state.
58			AutoInit: gh.Ptr(false),
59		})

67	// InitialCommit writes the first commit of an empty repository.
68	//
69	// It is four calls rather than one per file, and that is the whole design:
70	// Repositories.CreateFile in a loop would produce one commit per file, so a
71	// three-file template would arrive as three commits — and the second would need
72	// the SHA the first returned, which is a chain rather than a batch.
73	//
74	// The git data API takes the whole thing at once: a blob per file, one tree, a
75	// commit with **no parent**, then the ref that makes it the branch. No parent
76	// is what makes this an *initial* commit; on a repository that already has one
77	// the ref creation fails, which is the honest outcome — this is not a way to
78	// overwrite history.
79	func (f *Forge) InitialCommit(ctx context.Context, repositoryID string, files []forge.FileChange) error {
80		owner, repo, ok := splitPath(repositoryID)
81		if !ok {
82			return fmt.Errorf("not a GitHub repository: %q", repositoryID)
83		}
84		if len(files) == 0 {
85			return nil
86		}
87	
88		entries := make([]*gh.TreeEntry, 0, len(files))
89		for _, file := range files {
90			if file.Action == forge.FileDelete {
91				// There is nothing to delete in a repository with no commits, and
92				// silently dropping it would hide a template that means something
93				// else than it says.
94				return fmt.Errorf("an initial commit cannot delete %q", file.Path)
95			}
96	
97			blob, _, err := f.client.Git.CreateBlob(ctx, owner, repo, &gh.Blob{
98				Content:  gh.Ptr(file.Content),
99				Encoding: gh.Ptr("utf-8"),
100			})
101			if err != nil {
102				return fmt.Errorf("uploading %s: %w", file.Path, err)
103			}
104	
105			entries = append(entries, &gh.TreeEntry{
106				Path: gh.Ptr(file.Path),
107				Mode: gh.Ptr("100644"),
108				Type: gh.Ptr("blob"),
109				SHA:  blob.SHA,
110			})
111		}
112	
113		// No base tree: the repository is empty, and naming one that does not exist
114		// is an error rather than an empty starting point.
115		tree, _, err := f.client.Git.CreateTree(ctx, owner, repo, "", entries)
116		if err != nil {
117			return fmt.Errorf("building the tree: %w", err)
118		}
119	
120		commit, _, err := f.client.Git.CreateCommit(ctx, owner, repo, &gh.Commit{
121			Message: gh.Ptr(initialCommitMessage),
122			Tree:    tree,
123		}, nil)
124		if err != nil {
125			return fmt.Errorf("creating the commit: %w", err)
126		}
127	
128		_, _, err = f.client.Git.CreateRef(ctx, owner, repo, &gh.Reference{
129			Ref:    gh.Ptr("refs/heads/" + defaultBranch),
130			Object: &gh.GitObject{SHA: commit.SHA},
131		})
132		if err != nil {
133			return fmt.Errorf("creating %s: %w", defaultBranch, err)
134		}
135		return nil
136	}
137	
138	const (
139		// initialCommitMessage is the GitLab backend's, word for word: a template
140		// applied on either platform should read the same in the log.
141		initialCommitMessage = "Initial commit from template"
142	
143		// defaultBranch matches what both backends create. GitHub's per-account
144		// default is configurable, but a repository created here has no commits
145		// yet, so nothing has chosen a branch — naming it is the only way this is
146		// deterministic.
147		defaultBranch = "main"
148	)

153		if permanently {
154			return errNoPermanentDelete
155		}
156		owner, name, ok := splitPath(repo.ID)
157		if !ok {
158			return fmt.Errorf("not a GitHub repository: %q", repo.ID)
159		}
160		_, err := f.client.Repositories.Delete(ctx, owner, name)

164	// DashboardStats fetches the five counters.
165	//
166	// Four of them come from the **search** API, which is what GitHub offers
167	// instead of GitLab's X-Total header — and which has its own, much lower rate
168	// limit. Each is filled only when its request succeeded; a failed one stays nil
169	// rather than reading as a zero the dashboard would render as "you have none"
170	// (D52).
171	func (f *Forge) DashboardStats(ctx context.Context, user forge.User) (forge.DashboardStats, error) {
172		if user.Username == "" {
173			return forge.DashboardStats{}, errors.New("dashboard stats: no user")
174		}
175	
176		var stats forge.DashboardStats
177		one := &gh.SearchOptions{ListOptions: gh.ListOptions{PerPage: 1}}
178	
179		// Total is what these are for; the single result is discarded.
180		if result, _, err := f.client.Search.Issues(ctx,
181			"is:open is:pr assignee:"+user.Username, one); err == nil {
182			stats.AssignedChangeRequests = forge.Count(result.GetTotal())
183		}
184	
185		if result, _, err := f.client.Search.Issues(ctx,
186			"is:open is:pr review-requested:"+user.Username, one); err == nil {
187			stats.ReviewChangeRequests = forge.Count(result.GetTotal())
188		}
189	
190		if result, _, err := f.client.Search.Issues(ctx,
191			"is:open is:issue assignee:"+user.Username, one); err == nil {
192			stats.AssignedIssues = forge.Count(result.GetTotal())
193		}
194	
195		// Repositories and organisations have no search counterpart, so they are
196		// walked. Both are bounded by what one account belongs to, which is not the
197		// unbounded list a search would be.
198		if repos, err := listAll(func(page *gh.ListOptions) ([]*gh.Repository, *gh.Response, error) {
199			return f.client.Repositories.ListByAuthenticatedUser(ctx,
200				&gh.RepositoryListByAuthenticatedUserOptions{ListOptions: *page})
201		}); err == nil {
202			stats.Repositories = forge.Count(len(repos))
203		}
204	
205		if orgs, err := listAll(func(page *gh.ListOptions) ([]*gh.Organization, *gh.Response, error) {
206			return f.client.Organizations.List(ctx, "", page)
207		}); err == nil {
208			stats.Namespaces = forge.Count(len(orgs))
209		}
210	
211		return stats, nil
212	}

2	//
3	// It is the one place that knows both backends exist, and the only reason it is
4	// a package of its own: internal/forge must not import a backend (a domain
5	// package cannot depend on its implementations), and a backend must not import
6	// its sibling. Something above both has to choose, and this is it.
7	//
8	// The credential store is **not** forge-shaped — Storage is keyed on a URL and
9	// knows nothing else — so the loading and forgetting of a token are the same
10	// code whichever platform the context targets. Only opening a session differs,
11	// and only in which constructor it calls.
12	package session
13	
14	import (
15		"context"
16		"fmt"
17	
18		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/config"
19		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/credentials"
20		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/forge"
21		githubforge "github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/forge/github"
22		gitlabforge "github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/forge/gitlab"
23	)

25	// Auth opens sessions against a host and remembers their tokens.
26	type Auth struct {
27		storage credentials.Storage
28	}
29	
30	// NewAuth builds an Auth over a secret store. A nil store is legitimate: the
31	// session still opens, and nothing is remembered.
32	func NewAuth(storage credentials.Storage) *Auth {
33		return &Auth{storage: storage}
34	}
35	
36	// Result is a live session, plus whatever could not be saved about it.
37	type Result struct {
38		Forge forge.Forge
39		User  forge.User
40		// SaveWarning is set when the session opened but the token could not be
41		// stored. It is not an error: the session is valid, only its persistence
42		// failed, and telling the user they are not logged in would be false.
43		SaveWarning string
44	}
45	
46	// Backend builds a client for a platform, without opening a session.
47	//
48	// The default is GitLab, matching config.applyDefaults: an unknown type has
49	// already been normalised by the time a context is loaded, and falling through
50	// to the one backend that has always existed is better than returning an error
51	// nothing can act on.
52	func Backend(forgeType, url, token string) (forge.Forge, error) {
53		switch forgeType {
54		case config.ForgeGitHub:
55			return githubforge.New(url, token)
56		default:
57			return gitlabforge.New(url, token)
58		}
59	}
60	
61	// Authenticate opens a session and saves the token.
62	func (a *Auth) Authenticate(ctx context.Context, forgeType, url, token string) (*Result, error) {
63		result, err := a.AuthenticateOnly(ctx, forgeType, url, token)
64		if err != nil {
65			return nil, err
66		}
67	
68		if a.storage != nil {
69			if err := a.storage.Save(url, token); err != nil {
70				result.SaveWarning = fmt.Sprintf("The token was not saved: %v. You will have to enter it again next launch.", err)
71			}
72		}
73	
74		return result, nil
75	}
76	
77	// AuthenticateOnly opens a session and writes nothing. It is the auto-login
78	// path, whose token already comes from the store.
79	func (a *Auth) AuthenticateOnly(ctx context.Context, forgeType, url, token string) (*Result, error) {
80		backend, err := Backend(forgeType, url, token)
81		if err != nil {
82			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to create client: %w", err)
83		}
84	
85		// CurrentUser is the connection test: authentication succeeded exactly when
86		// the host answers with who the token belongs to.
87		user, err := backend.CurrentUser(ctx)
88		if err != nil {
89			return nil, fmt.Errorf("authentication failed: %w", err)
90		}
91	
92		return &Result{Forge: backend, User: user}, nil
93	}
94	
95	// LoadCredentials reads a stored token.
96	//
97	// It takes no forge type, and that is not an oversight: the store is keyed on
98	// the URL, so a context that switched platform without changing host finds the
99	// token it already had — which is right, because it is the same host asking.
100	func (a *Auth) LoadCredentials(url string) (string, error) {
101		if a.storage == nil {
102			return "", fmt.Errorf("no storage configured")
103		}
104		return a.storage.Load(url)
105	}
106	
107	// Logout forgets a stored token.
108	func (a *Auth) Logout(url string) error {
109		if a.storage == nil {
110			return nil
111		}
112		return a.storage.Delete(url)
113	}

5	// Vocabulary is what a forge is *called*, as opposed to what it can do.
6	//
7	// The distinction is §3.6's: "Group" against "Organization" is a **word**,
8	// while nesting depth and the visibility set are **shapes** — they change what
9	// the application can promise, and no wording helps with them. Shape carries
10	// the second; this carries the first, and neither grows conditionals for the
11	// other.
12	//
13	// # Per forge, not neutral
14	//
15	// A GitLab user says *group*, a GitHub user says *repository*. "Namespace" is a
16	// third language nobody speaks, and it makes the application read as an
17	// abstraction layer rather than as a tool. So every word here is the one its
18	// forge's own documentation uses.
19	//
20	// The field names are neutral because the *code* has to be — a view cannot
21	// switch on which forge it is talking to — but nothing a user reads is.
22	//
23	// # No view writes a forge's name into a string
24	//
25	// That is the rule this type exists to make checkable, and
26	// TestNoViewNamesAForge (internal/ui/vocabtest) walks every string literal
27	// under internal/ui to enforce it. A command name is not covered: it is routing
28	// identity, the same for both forges, and lives in internal/command.
29	type Vocabulary struct {
30		// Name is the forge as it names itself — "GitLab", "GitHub". Capitalised:
31		// it is a proper noun, and it is what titles and messages interpolate.
32		Name string
33	
34		// Namespace holds repositories and, on some forges, other namespaces.
35		Namespace, Namespaces string
36	
37		// Repository is one repository.
38		Repository, Repositories string
39	
40		// ChangeRequest is a proposal to merge a branch.
41		ChangeRequest, ChangeRequests string
42	
43		// ChangeRequestShort is the initialism — "MR", "PR". The dashboard's tree
44		// nodes are eleven cells wide, so the long form does not fit and truncating
45		// it would produce "Merge Req…" on one forge and "Pull Requ…" on the other.
46		ChangeRequestShort string
47	
48		// TokenLabel is what the auth view calls the secret it asks for.
49		TokenLabel string
50	
51		// TokenPlaceholder is an example token, shown greyed in the input until the
52		// user types.
53		//
54		// It is a hint and never a check: DevDesk does not validate the prefix, and
55		// a forge that changes its format must not turn a working token into a
56		// refused one. Shaped like a real value rather than as prose, because that
57		// is what a placeholder is — the prose about which prefixes exist lives in
58		// TokenHelp, where there is room to name more than one.
59		TokenPlaceholder string
60	
61		// TokenHelp says where to create a token and which scopes it needs. One
62		// sentence, because it is rendered in a help pane beside others.
63		TokenHelp string
64	
65		// ExampleURL is what the configuration view suggests as a host. The public
66		// instance, because it is the only address that is the same for everyone —
